solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Get elected introducing key source of green electricity (4,5)

indicatorNotes.introducing: the phrase for getting elected introduces a letter into its middle

blocks.note: to win power is to get elected
D is a musical key

annotation.surface: A candidate brings a key renewable energy policy into office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get elected' has to be rephrased as a two-word idiom before the key can be slotted between its words; the answer's own enumeration, (4,5), hints at where the split falls.
annotation.definitionFit: Wind power is electricity generated by turbines, a renewable, green source.

entries.clue: Like many presents wife criticised (7)

blocks.note: w = wife, from marriage records
to rap is to criticise sharply

annotation.surface: A wife finds fault with the gifts she has been given.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'presents' the gifts the wife criticised; in fact 'Like many presents' is the whole definition, describing the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Most presents come wrapped in paper.

entries.clue: Nothing American escapes arrest (3)

indicatorNotes.escapes: the American gets away, so its letter leaves the word

blocks.note: to nail a suspect is to arrest them
A = American, removed

annotation.surface: An American suspect gets clean away, so the police have nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a fugitive slipping the police; 'arrest' has to be a verb meaning NAIL, which loses its A.
annotation.definitionFit: Nil means nothing, especially as a score.

entries.clue: Humorous theatre in the East End? (8)

indicatorNotes.the East End: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their H's

blocks.note: plays are theatre, drama on stage
in = at HOME; said in the East End, it loses its H

annotation.surface: A question about whether a comedy theatre might be found in east London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' meaning at home is the hard step: HOME becomes 'OME because London's East End is the home of the Cockney accent, which drops the H.
annotation.definitionFit: Playsome is an old word for playful, so humorous in a light-hearted way.

entries.clue: Small county flags (5)

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation of a county in south-west England
to flag is to droop or tire

annotation.surface: A little county puts out its bunting.
annotation.walkthrough: Wilts is the short form of Wiltshire, a county in south-west England, which is why 'Small' belongs to the definition. 'Flags' is a verb, not bunting.
annotation.definitionFit: Wilts abbreviates Wiltshire, and a plant that wilts flags or droops.

entries.clue: Sells tickets to win one first-class big-flowered plant (9)

blocks.note: to raffle something is to sell tickets for a chance to win it
I = one, the Roman numeral
A = first-class, as in A1 or grade A

annotation.surface: Someone runs a raffle with a prize-winning showy plant as the prize.
annotation.walkthrough: RAFFLES needs the whole phrase 'Sells tickets to win', not just 'Sells'.
annotation.definitionFit: Rafflesia is a parasitic plant with the largest single flower in the world.

entries.clue: Leave nought as capital (5)

blocks.note: to quit is to leave
O looks like nought

annotation.surface: An instruction to leave a zero standing as money, or as a capital letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a large letter; it is a capital city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ecuador's seat of government, high in the Andes, is one of many capital cities.

entries.clue: Book Torquay, mostly touring (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.touring: the letters travel around into a new order

blocks.note: Torquay without its final Y

annotation.surface: A travel note about reserving a holiday in Torquay, a seaside resort in Devon, and mostly driving around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book' sits first as if it were a verb for reserving a holiday; it is the noun, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book made from sheets folded twice into four leaves.

entries.clue: Oil in tin can awkwardly leaning (11)

indicatorNotes.awkwardly: the letters are placed clumsily, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: An oil can standing awkwardly at an angle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the oil inside the can; it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean a tendency or preference, and both also carry the literal sense of a slope or tilt.

entries.clue: Reticent ones unknown among market traders taking the lead (7)

indicatorNotes.among: the unknown sits among the other letters
indicatorNotes.taking the lead: the traders have their lead letter taken away

blocks.note: COSTERS, costermongers, minus their first letter C
Y = an unknown, as in algebra

annotation.surface: Quiet types, unknown among the street traders, step up to lead.
annotation.walkthrough: Costers, short for costermongers, are British street sellers of fruit and vegetables. 'Taking the lead' sounds like going first, but here the lead letter is taken off.
annotation.definitionFit: An oyster is a byword for a close-mouthed, reticent person, one who says nothing.

entries.clue: How people greeted extreme wintry forecast? (3,4)

blocks.note: an old formal greeting
a forecast of hail and nothing else

annotation.surface: A question about how the public took news of a very harsh weather forecast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks how people reacted to a forecast; the answer is both an old greeting and a forecast of nothing but hail.
annotation.definitionFit: 'All hail!' was a formal greeting, as the witches greet Macbeth.

entries.clue: Saint Africans beheaded cruelly (7)

indicatorNotes.beheaded: the head, the first letter, is cut off
indicatorNotes.cruelly: the remaining letters are treated roughly, out of order

blocks.note: AFRICANS without its first letter A

annotation.surface: A grim story of a saint whose African followers were cruelly executed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as martyrdom, which suits a saint; the beheading happens to the word, not to people.
annotation.definitionFit: Francis is a saint, most famously Francis of Assisi.

entries.clue: Motorway’s ending in interchange to the west part of Wales (5)

indicatorNotes.ending: only the last letter of the word is used
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes inside the interchange
indicatorNotes.to the west: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

blocks.note: swop is a British spelling of swap, an interchange
the last letter of motorway

annotation.surface: Directions: at the end of the motorway, take the interchange west into Wales.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interchange' looks like a motorway junction, fitting the surface, but it means a swap, here spelt SWOP.
annotation.definitionFit: Powys is a large county in central Wales.

entries.clue: Spa’s energy restored to health very fast (4-7)

blocks.note: a well is a spring or spa; the 's adds S
E = energy, as in physics
cured = restored to health

annotation.surface: A spa's energetic treatment brings people back to health in no time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very fast' reads as speed, but fast here means firmly fixed, as in 'stuck fast'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something well-secured is held very fast, firmly fixed in place.

entries.clue: Puzzle of old drunk found in southern river (9)

indicatorNotes.found in: the old drunk is found inside the southern river

blocks.note: S = southern
O = old
lit = drunk, slang
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

annotation.surface: The mystery of an old drunk discovered in a river down south.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a crime story with a body in the water; 'Puzzle' is the definition, not a comment on the mystery.
annotation.definitionFit: Solitaire is a one-player puzzle game, pegs jumped on a board or cards laid out.

entries.clue: I’m back in Toledo’s fantastic mountains (9)

indicatorNotes.back: I'M is turned back to front
indicatorNotes.in: the turned letters go inside the anagram
indicatorNotes.fantastic: the letters of Toledo's are rearranged wildly

blocks.note: anagram fodder, including the S of the 's
I'M, reversed to MI

annotation.surface: A traveller returning to Toledo in Spain praises its fantastic mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of Toledo's is part of the fodder, not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dolomites are a mountain range in north-east Italy.

entries.clue: Drunken behaviour ends entertaining functions (9)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain is to take in, so ends hold the functions

blocks.note: tips = ends, points
sines are trigonometric functions

annotation.surface: A party's drunken antics finally put an end to the entertainment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Functions' look like parties, which suits the drunken surface; they are mathematical functions.
annotation.definitionFit: Tipsiness is the state of being tipsy, slightly drunk.

entries.clue: I’m not responding to that amorous advance (4)

annotation.definitionNote: the first definition is a whole utterance, which PASS is when said in a quiz

blocks.note: what a quiz contestant says to skip a question
the romantic move someone 'makes at' another person

annotation.surface: Someone turning down a romantic approach.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface joins the two halves into one rejection; they are separate: the quiz-show 'Pass' and making a pass at someone.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying 'Pass' declines to answer, and a pass is a romantic advance.

entries.clue: Water additive a cause of potential damage at Aquae Sulis? (4,4)

annotation.definition2: a cause of potential damage at Aquae Sulis?

blocks.note: a fizzing ball dropped into bathwater

blocks.clueFragment: a cause of potential damage at Aquae Sulis?
blocks.note: a bomb in Bath, the city the Romans called Aquae Sulis

annotation.surface: A question about what might have damaged the Roman baths at Bath.
annotation.walkthrough: Aquae Sulis is the Roman name for Bath, an English spa city; an explosive device there would be a Bath bomb. The question mark flags this playful second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A bath bomb is a fizzing ball of scent and salts dropped into bathwater.

entries.clue: British demand to lie in the sun (4)

blocks.note: B = British
to ask is to demand

annotation.surface: The British insistence on sunbathing on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long demand; the definition starts only after 'to'.
annotation.definitionFit: To bask is to lie enjoying warmth, especially the sun.

entries.clue: Loudly criticise pub’s space for glasses? (7)

blocks.note: a bar is a pub; the 's means 'has'
a rack is where glasses are stored

annotation.surface: A complaint about the pub's shelving for glasses.
annotation.walkthrough: To barrack is British and Australian for jeering a speaker or player. 'Glasses' suggests spectacles; it is drinking glasses.
annotation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer or shout criticism at someone.

entries.clue: Putting coat on outside a cape is soothing (9)

indicatorNotes.outside: the coating goes outside, around, the other letters

blocks.note: plating is putting a coat of metal on
A as written
C = cape, on maps

annotation.surface: Someone finds putting a coat over a cape comforting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coat' suggests clothing, matching 'cape'; here it is a metal coating, and cape is a headland.
annotation.definitionFit: Placating someone is soothing them, calming their anger.

entries.clue: Unappealing lees at bottom in reserve port (7)

indicatorNotes.at bottom: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

blocks.note: grim = unappealing
the bottom letter of lees
something put by is kept in reserve

annotation.surface: Unpleasant dregs left at the bottom of some reserve port wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about port the drink, with its lees; the answer is a port on the sea. Grimsby is a fishing port in north-east England.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Humber estuary town was once the busiest fishing harbour in the world.

entries.clue: Print small book (6)

blocks.note: roman is the ordinary upright print, as opposed to italic
S = small, as in clothing sizes

annotation.surface: An instruction to publish a short book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Print' looks like a verb; it is the typeface.
annotation.definitionFit: Romans, Paul's Epistle to the Romans, is a book of the New Testament.

entries.clue: Ministers’ housing concerning Conservative politicians (9)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in memo headers
C = Conservative
Tories are Conservative politicians in Britain

annotation.surface: A news item on housing policy that affects government ministers and Conservative MPs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' suggests government; here they are ministers of religion. Tories is the nickname for members of Britain's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a church minister.

entries.clue: Dignified honour accepted by senior (5)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: the senior takes the honour in, holding it inside

blocks.note: Sr = senior
OBE, Order of the British Empire, a British honour

annotation.surface: An elderly person receives a royal honour with quiet dignity.
annotation.walkthrough: An OBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Sober means serious and dignified in manner.

entries.clue: Language heard in North Dakota and Iowa primarily (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take only the primary, first, letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of heard, in, North, Dakota
first letter of Iowa

annotation.surface: A remark that some language is spoken in two Midwestern states.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heard' looks like a sound-alike signal, and it is only a word whose first letter counts; 'and' joins without contributing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is the most widely spoken tongue of India, written in Devanagari script.

entries.clue: Some land and race round in time (7)

indicatorNotes.round: the letters of race are turned round into a new order
indicatorNotes.in: 'in time' means within a period, so the rearranged letters sit inside the word for time

blocks.note: an age is a period of time
rearranged to CREA

annotation.surface: A plot of land, and someone racing around it against the clock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Race round' sounds like running a lap, and 'Some land' reads as the start of a list; both are traps, since the definition is the opening two words alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Acreage is an amount of land measured in acres.

entries.clue: Audibly disapprove of neckwear and footwear (7)

blocks.note: to boo is to disapprove out loud
ties are worn round the neck

annotation.surface: Someone jeering at another's fashion choices from head to toe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audibly' looks like a sound-alike signal, but BOO is simply the noise of disapproval.
annotation.definitionFit: Booties are soft shoes or ankle boots.

entries.clue: Agency working in US reserve (3)

blocks.note: Immigration and Customs Enforcement
reserve as coldness of manner, what gets broken at a party

annotation.surface: A US government agency in its reserve role.
annotation.walkthrough: ICE is US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. 'Reserve' is coolness of manner, the ice in 'break the ice'.
annotation.definitionFit: The first is an acronym for a federal immigration body; the second is figurative, coldness of manner as in 'break the ice'.

entries.clue: Country recalled party’s prestige (5)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the UK, turned to KU
a do is a party; the 's adds S

annotation.surface: A nation withdraws its ambassador, damaging a political party's standing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests an ambassador summoned home; it reverses only the country.
annotation.definitionFit: Kudos is prestige or praise earned by an achievement.

entries.clue: Able to stretch out by quiet area of garden (9)

indicatorNotes.by: one piece sits beside the other

blocks.note: sh = quiet
rubbery things stretch

annotation.surface: A garden spot quiet enough to stretch out and relax in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stretch out' suggests lounging in the garden; it describes elastic material.
annotation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is a part of a garden planted with shrubs.
